messages:
sophie: quick followup from the autoscale RFC: i've been noodling on a compact probe-hint token the control plane can hand to operators so evictions can be latency-aware without pulling large policy blobs. want to sanity-check assumptions.

matt: curious what you mean by compact token. a few bytes or a signed blob?

sophie: minimal fields: model_family, warmup_delta_ms, p95_delta_pct, expires_at, signature. something like: `{"mf":"llama-2-13b","wd":120,"p95":18,"exp":1710000000,"sig":"..."}`. operator trusts sig chain and applies a local smoothing window.

anya: why not include a confidence score? probing is noisy for small sample sizes.

sophie: good call. add `conf` (0..1). control plane will only emit token if conf >= 0.6 by default.

raj: where do probes run? running them on shared GPUs is dangerous.

sophie: probes run in isolated sandboxes on CPU-hosted containers or dedicated tiny GPU slices. they never touch real tenant data; payloads are synthetic short prompts.

liz: operational concern: a malicious tenant could try to flood probes to bias hints. need rate limits and per-tenant caps.

sophie: agreed. probe trigger budget is per-pool and per-model-family. each tenant can only request probes indirectly via control-plane heuristics; we cap influence with an exponential smoothing across all tenants.

matt: operator behaviour: what if control plane tokens expire or CP unreachable?

sophie: operator fallback rules: 1) if token expired and no recent history -> conservative_preempt_window (e.g., 500ms no-preempt), 2) if high util (>92% for >90s) -> bypass latency blocks (emergency preempt), 3) if signed hint present -> apply hint score but clamp by tenant max_override.

anya: how do we measure warmup_delta_ms? wallclock of first token vs steady-state token? that's brittle across models and batch sizes.

sophie: we measure a short sequence of micro-benchmarks: single-token generation with the same batching profile used in production. warmup_delta = observed start latency - baseline steady latency. we keep rolling-window percentiles (p50/p95).

raj: testing/rollout: i'd like a staging sim that replays historical traffic and runs the hinting logic offline first. don't let operator act on hints until sim results are sane.

sophie: yep plan: (1) simulation/offline audit for 14 days, (2) opt-in staging operator mode (no evictions, only metrics), (3) soft-enforce (evictions allowed but flagged and counters incremented), (4) global enable.

liz: what metrics do we expose? need `hint_emitted`, `hint_age`, `probe_rps`, `blocked_evictions_count`, `emergency_bypasses`.

sophie: agree. also add `hint_mismatch_alerts` when operator bypasses a hint more than X% — helps catch drift.

matt: ownership: controller team owns probe emitter and token signer. operator team owns token verifier and fallback circuit. docs will define the token schema and TTL.

anya: small ops question: TTL should account for clock skew. let's keep token TTL >= 30s and allow operator to accept leeway of +/- 5s.

sophie: noted. default TTL=45s, max TTL enforceable by operator policy.

liz: one more safety: when operator sees many small tokens for different model families, it should merge hints to avoid thrashing decisions. define `merged_score = weighted_avg(score, recency)`.

sophie: will add hint-merge pseudocode in RFC. also adding an operator debug endpoint to dump active hints for incident triage.

controller-bot: policy-controller v0.53.0 deployed to staging at 1767123560 (triggered by sophie).

raj: next step: sophie update RFC with token spec, probe sandboxing plan, rollout sim plan. ping infra for replay dataset. i'll schedule a 30m sync to review metrics mapping.

sophie: thanks — i'll file the update by EOD and attach a data sample for the sim. :thumbsup:
